title: ChatRelay — Connect From Anywhere
objective: ChatRelay authenticates a WebSocket connection using your session cookie at connect time. Show that a connection opened as if from a completely different website is still accepted and authenticated.

verifier.condition: A WebSocket connection whose handshake carried an Origin header for a different site than this application completes and is treated as an authenticated session.

weakness: The WebSocket upgrade handler authenticates using the session cookie but never checks the handshake's Origin header, so a page on any other website can open an authenticated connection on a visiting user's behalf — the browser attaches cookies to a WebSocket handshake the same way it does to an ordinary request.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /chat (WebSocket upgrade; Origin header never checked)
seededData: A real WebSocket server (the ws / @fastify/websocket packages — not a simulated protocol). One chat session cookie, minted via normal login.

credentials.label: Chat user
credentials.note: Sign in first to get a session cookie, then open a WebSocket connection yourself.

hints: Open a normal WebSocket connection to /chat after signing in and confirm it works and greets you by name.
This time, open the connection while sending an Origin header for a completely unrelated site — your session cookie still goes along with it, the same as any other request to this host.
Browsers attach cookies to WebSocket handshakes exactly as they do to regular HTTP requests, regardless of which page initiated the connection.
burpNotes: Burp's WebSocket support (or a scripted ws client) lets you set arbitrary handshake headers, including Origin, while still sending your real session cookie.
